Start a normal game with a random secret.

    cargo run --locked --

The game draws one number from 1 to 100. The draw carries no guarantee of cryptographic randomness or a reproducible sequence across versions of rand.

Use a fixed secret for a reproducible exercise transcript.

The --attempts N option accepts one to twenty attempts and defaults to six. Invalid configuration prints usage to stderr and exits with code 2 before the game starts.

# Design and boundaries

The parser is pure. Game owns the secret and the state. Only play connects buffered input to terminal output. Once the attempt count has been validated, a valid draw occurs exactly once. Incorrect guesses and invalid inputs never trigger another draw.

The adapter reads at most 129 bytes at a time so it can detect an overlong line without reading the remainder. This bounds the adapter's temporary buffer. A custom BufRead can allocate more memory within its own implementation. Terminal write and flush failures propagate as I/O errors. Data written before an error remains observable.

## Files and public API

- `src/command.rs` defines `Command`, `CommandError`, and `parse_command(&str)`.
- `src/todo.rs` defines `Todo::new()` and `Todo::apply(Command)`.
- `src/storage.rs` defines `FormatError`, `StorageError`, `encode(&Todo)`, `decode(&str)`, `load(&str)`, and `save(&str, &Todo)`.
- `src/app.rs` defines `AppError` and `execute(&str, &str)`.
- `src/main.rs` handles the path argument, stdin, stdout, stderr, and exit code.
- `tests/cli.rs` tests the public API and real program processes.

`Todo` keeps its state private to library callers. `Task` and its fields use `pub(crate)` so storage can reconstruct the data within the same crate. Keep that visibility. `#[derive(...)]` supplies implementations such as Debug and comparisons, so custom traits or generic functions are unnecessary. Import `std::io::Write` explicitly to access `write_all`. `sync_all` is a method on `File`.

## Commands and state

`parse_command` calls `trim` on the entire line and splits at the first ordinary space. A tab cannot separate the verb from its argument. Verbs are lowercase.

- `add tytuł` trims the edges of the title, preserves its interior, and returns `Command::Add(String)`. An empty title or embedded LF or CR gives `InvalidTitle`.
- `done N` takes a positive `usize` written with ASCII digits. Leading zeros are valid. Zero, a plus or minus sign, non-ASCII digits, and overflow give `InvalidId`.
- `list` accepts only an empty argument. Extra text gives `Unknown`.
- An empty line gives `Empty`. Other commands give `Unknown`.

`Todo::new()` is empty. Calling `apply(Add(title))` directly revalidates the title but stores it exactly as supplied, including edge spaces. Duplicate titles are valid. IDs start at 1 and follow row order. Add returns `added N`. Done(0) gives `InvalidId`, and an ID beyond the list gives `NotFound`. Errors leave state intact. A valid Done returns `done N`, even when repeated. List returns an empty String or rows of the form `N [ ] title\n` / `N [x] title\n`.

## Exact file format

The first line is exactly `RUST_TODO_V1\n`. Each following line is `0\ttitle\n` for an incomplete task or `1\ttitle\n` for a completed task. Here `\t` denotes one literal tab and `\n` one LF. The file encoding is UTF-8. Example bytes as a Rust string literal follow.

```rust
"RUST_TODO_V1\n0\tplan\n1\tZażółć  🙂\n"
```

An empty Todo is a header-only file. Every line, including the last, ends with LF. Reject a BOM before the header, CR and CRLF, blank lines, and comments. The status is exactly `0` or `1`. Split a row only at the first tab. Further tabs belong to the title. The title must remain nonempty after `trim`, and stored spaces, tabs, and Unicode must be preserved. The title may contain neither LF nor CR. Row order determines IDs, which have no separate field.

`decode` validates in this order.

1. Require the exact header with LF, otherwise return `InvalidHeader`.
2. Require a final LF for the file, otherwise return `MissingFinalNewline`.
3. Visit rows in order. A missing tab gives `InvalidRow(n)`, an unrecognized status gives `InvalidStatus(n)`, and an invalid title gives `InvalidTitle(n)`.

`n` is the physical line number. The first task is on line 2. Return the first error in the stated order. Split on `\n` and preserve CR for validation, since `lines()` strips CR from CRLF endings.

## Loading, saving, and execution

`load` returns an empty Todo only on `ErrorKind::NotFound` and creates no file in that case. It returns other read errors, including invalid UTF-8, as `StorageError::Io` and invalid format as `StorageError::Format`.

`save` appends `.tmp` to the whole path, for example `tasks.todo.tmp` beside `tasks.todo`. Use `create_new(true)`, then `write_all`, then `sync_all`, then close the handle with `drop`, then `rename` to the destination. An existing temporary file is an error. Leave it intact. A failure before rename preserves the previous data file. Once you have created your own temporary file, try to remove it after any later error. Return the original error even if cleanup fails.

The protocol has no full durability guarantee after a system crash or power loss and does not coordinate concurrent writers. `sync_all` applies to the temporary file and the workshop does not synchronize the directory after rename. Run one writer per file. Inspect a `.tmp` left after interruption and remove it manually only after confirming no active process owns it. Never delete another writer's file automatically to bypass an error.

`execute(path, line)` parses first and loads fresh state for every call. It invokes `apply` and saves only successful Add and Done commands, including repeated Done. It returns success text only after saving succeeds. List and command errors never write. `AppError::Command` wraps parser or model errors. `AppError::Storage` wraps read, format, or write errors.

```sh
cargo run --offline -- "tasks.todo"
```

## Contracts

- `reserve(&AtomicUsize, amount, limit)` returns Some with the previous value if the entire reservation fits within both limit and usize. Otherwise it returns None and leaves the counter unchanged. - `publication()` creates one non-cloneable Publisher and a cloneable Subscriber. `publish(self, value)` consumes the right to write. Every usize, including 0 and MAX, is a valid message. The Subscriber tries once. None means it observed no publication. Some must contain the published value. Each Publisher can send only once.
- Dropping the Publisher without publishing leaves readers with None. The API makes no distinction between waiting and abandonment. It provides no blocking, wakeup, or bounded completion guarantee. Contention may cause the CAS loop to retry without a fairness guarantee.

# ADR: jeden niezmiennik na protokół\n\n.en:
# ADR — One invariant per protocol

This decision applies to the lab. Use established primitives for production systems.

## Reservation

The counter tracks occupied units only. A successful reservation stays within the limit and returns the value immediately preceding its update. For a global limit, all participants must agree on the same value. The counter publishes no other data. Relaxed is sufficient for a CAS to update one atomic cell. After an Err from CAS, recompute the sum and check the limit against the newly observed value. Never reuse the old next.

A Mutex would simplify an update touching several fields or a more involved rejection path. Evaluating CAS performance would require a separate hypothesis, workload, and measurements under contention.

## Publication

The Publisher alone can write, and publishing consumes that capability. The payload is immutable after publication.

1. The sender writes value with Relaxed.
2. The sender writes true to ready with Release.
3. The receiver reads that true from ready with Acquire.
4. The receiver then reads value with Relaxed.

Synchronization occurs when the Acquire reads from the corresponding Release. That sequence orders the earlier write before the later payload read. Since ready never returns to false and there is only one sender, the true value identifies that publication. The payload is also atomic, so the flawed variant can return an incorrect value without introducing UB.

This design rules out Relaxed on the flag, joining before the model assertion, and resetting ready for another message without a new protocol. SeqCst imposes stronger ordering, but multiple senders would still require a different protocol. An existing channel has a broader contract and suits production message passing.

## Evidence boundaries

Ordinary tests check the API and boundary values. Loom models small scenarios through instrumented types. Intentional counterexamples must fail so we know the assertions detect the defects. Keep the happens-before argument, the analysis of larger protocols, dependency review, and measurements as independent evidence.

# Lab — Tokio pipeline

Design a work queue with a bounded buffer and a separate bound on active tasks. Shutdown must account for each accepted message as a success, domain error, timeout, or panic. This lab follows the Tokio lessons and targets local learning.

## Setup

Use stable Rust with support for edition 2024. Tokio is pinned to 1.54.1 and Cargo.lock records the dependency graph. The initial fetch requires a network connection.

```sh
cargo fetch --locked
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --offline --locked --all-targets
cargo test --offline --locked
cargo clippy --offline --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Implement `enqueue`, `spawn_pipeline`, and `run_pipeline` in src/lib.rs. The starter compiles and its tests intentionally fail at `todo!`. The reference passes tests and Clippy. Tests use real Tokio with a paused clock, so scenario durations do not translate into wall-clock waits. Keep the supplied tests intact.

Mastery requires independent lesson work beyond downloads, local tests, and checklists. Revealing the package records assistance for related tasks.

## Contract

- `Config.capacity` bounds the mpsc buffer. `parallelism` separately bounds active children. Both must be positive, and the capacity must fit within Tokio's mpsc limits. Receive no more work while all worker slots are occupied.
- `enqueue` takes `&mut Option<Job<T>>`. An empty slot succeeds even if the channel is closed. Reserve space before calling `take`. Cancellation while waiting or channel closure leaves the message with the caller. There is no await between `take` and sending through the Permit.
- Call `spawn_pipeline` inside a running Tokio runtime with time enabled. Each Job has its own task. The `process` factory is Send + Sync and shared through Arc. Clone is unnecessary. Evaluate `process(value)` inside the child so a panic from the call has an associated task ID.
- Each deadline starts when work begins, independent of time in the buffer. `Outcome` retains the owned result or domain error. Timing out drops the owned work Future. `JoinFailure` retains the full JoinError and panic payload.
- `shutdown(self)` signals stop, closes ordinary admission, drains the buffer, and collects every result without aborting tasks. Producers may keep Sender clones. A later ordinary send returns the unsent Job.
- A Permit obtained before close can still deliver a message. Shutdown waits for the Permit to be used or dropped. `is_closed()` alone cannot establish that draining is finished.
- Order the report by receipt at the receiver, even if children finish in another order. Public `Job.id` values may repeat. Use internal task identity to match each result, including a panic, to its report position.
- An empty queue shuts down cleanly. A child failure preserves the other results. A manager failure returns a separate `Err(JoinError)` from `shutdown` to distinguish it from a complete report.

## Boundaries

The buffer and work in flight are bounded. The report stores every result in a Vec, so total memory grows with the number of jobs. Streaming results requires a separate receive protocol and backpressure.

A timeout cannot preempt blocking code or a Future that takes a long time to yield. External effects persist. Sustained CPU work, blocking I/O, and retries with side effects require further design. Dropping Pipeline closes the oneshot to signal stop and detaches the manager's JoinHandle. Awaiting shutdown confirms completion. Cancelling that wait provides no confirmation.

This explains the reference lab. Add your own counterexample and alternative before revealing src/lib.rs.

## Ownership and bounds

The producer keeps its Job in an Option until it obtains a Permit. The manager owns the Receiver and JoinSet. On receipt, it records the child's internal identity and report position. The child owns the value and processing Future. Every outcome, including a panic, reaches the manager. The public Job.id serves as a label and can repeat.

One limit bounds the buffer and another bounds the task count. When all slots are occupied, the manager stops receiving. Spawning tasks before waiting for a semaphore would create an unbounded task queue. The Vec report stores every result and grows independently of both limits.

## Shutdown

Select uses explicit biased priority. It checks stop first, then a ready result, then new input. Disable the stop branch after its first observation so it cannot starve draining. Joins may briefly take priority, but every join removes one of a finite number of children. Permits acquired before close are part of the admission commitment. Call recv until it returns None.

Each child applies its timeout to the owned work Future. A timeout on the JoinHandle could leave the child running. Normal shutdown neither aborts the JoinSet nor exits on the first JoinError. It returns the complete report after draining and joining. Drop cannot await this protocol.

## Rejected shortcuts

- An unbounded channel hides overload in memory.
- Spawning tasks before limiting parallelism moves the backlog into tasks.
- Timing out a handle bounds only the wait and can leave independent work running.
- `join_all` can lose outcomes at the first panic. Joining in a loop retains each failure and its identity.
- Closing without draining loses accepted data and messages sent through earlier Permits.

# Lab — TCP service

Build a local Tokio service that accepts one request frame per TCP connection. The lab teaches ownership, admission, and shutdown boundaries with a local server.

## Setup

Use stable Rust with edition 2024. The package pins Tokio to exactly 1.54.1 and includes Cargo.lock. Fetching dependencies for the first time can require a network connection.

```sh
cargo fetch --locked
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --offline --locked --all-targets
cargo test --offline --locked
cargo clippy --offline --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo run --offline --locked
```

The starter compiles, but tests stop at intentional `todo!` calls. Keep the tests intact. The reference starts a local client and server on IPv4 loopback and stops them through explicit owner shutdown.

## Protocol and deadline

Each connection handles **exactly one** request frame and one response frame, then the handler closes the stream. A frame starts with a two-byte big-endian `u16` length followed by exactly that many payload bytes. TCP is a byte stream. A read can return any fragment and a write does not define a message boundary.

`max_frame_bytes` is a positive policy limit. Check input length before allocating a payload and output length before sending the header. Every response starts with a status byte, leaving at most `max_frame_bytes - 1` bytes for a successful processor payload. Distinguish clean EOF before the first byte, a truncated frame, an I/O error, a limit violation, and deadline expiry. A successful write or flush confirms local I/O only.

Each numeric limit must be positive and at most `Semaphore::MAX_PERMITS`. Set `request_deadline` above zero and at most `MAX_REQUEST_DEADLINE` (24 hours). Validate these limits before creating a listener or manager to avoid a channel or semaphore panic or an `Instant` overflow.

At handler entry, compute a single absolute deadline using `Instant`. Use it for reading the frame, waiting for queue space, waiting for blocking work, and writing the response. Terminate the connection at expiry. A partial read receives no new time budget, and a partially written frame cannot resume.

## Limits and ownership

- `admitted_connections` reserves a permit **before** `accept`. The handler owns it until it finishes with the socket. The kernel listen backlog is a separate queue and does not count active handlers.
- `queued_work` bounds `mpsc`. Handlers can wait for space. Admission already bounds their count, so waiting needs no separate task on a semaphore.
- `active_workers` bounds a separate `Semaphore`. The manager receives work only when its `JoinSet` has space and transfers the `OwnedSemaphorePermit` into the `spawn_blocking` closure.
- A dropped network waiter or client timeout can abandon the response oneshot. The manager still owns the started closure's `JoinHandle` and joins it. The worker permit stays with the running closure.

The processor is shared as `Arc<dyn Processor>`; user code needs no `Clone` implementation. The contract requires the processor closure to return on its own. There is no finite shutdown guarantee for arbitrary blocking code without cooperative cancellation.

## Responses and report

Each response has a distinct tag. `O || payload` means success, `E` a domain error, `J` a panic or cancelled closure, and `I` a manager invariant violation. The domain error is consumed at the worker-to-client boundary. The report keeps a `rejected` count and the manager keeps the full `JoinError` in `worker_join_failures`. I/O and protocol errors belong to `ConnectionOutcome`. This ownership scheme avoids duplicating a non-`Clone` domain error or `JoinError`.

`ServiceReport` retains all connection outcomes and JoinErrors. The limits bound current connections, the queue, and workers. Report memory grows with the number of handled connections. After a fatal accept error, join the accepted handlers before closing and draining the pool. If the manager itself fails unexpectedly, report `unstarted_after_manager_failure` and `started_may_remain_unjoined_after_manager_failure` to show that the drain may be incomplete.

## Shutdown

The owner of `serve_until` owns the stop signal. After stop, cease reserving admission permits, drop the listener, and join accepted handlers. Then drop the queue sender, drain the queue, and join all started blocking jobs. Dropping a `JoinHandle`, abandoning the oneshot, or timing out a wait does not prove completion. Use the shutdown protocol without aborting tasks.

## Counterexamples

1. Acquire a connection permit after `accept`. Clients can already be handed off to handlers beyond the limit.
2. Spawn before acquiring the worker semaphore. Waiting tasks can form an unbounded queue.
3. Keep the worker permit in the async waiter. A timeout admits another closure while the first still runs.
4. Reset the deadline for each `read`. Slow partial frames can exceed the total budget.
5. Stop after dropping the listener. Sockets, queued work, or unjoined closures can remain.

The three intentionally broken counterexamples in `tests/mutants.rs` compile and are ignored by the normal test suite. Each command should reach the specified failing assertion after releasing its test closures.

```sh

cargo test --offline --locked --test mutants dropping_a_blocking_handle_is_not_a_completed_shutdown -- --ignored --exact
```

# ADR — Who owns connections and blocking work?

This decision applies to the educational reference package.

## Decision

The protocol handles one frame per connection. At entry, the handler computes an absolute deadline. It terminates the stream on incomplete I/O or timeout. This gives the stream one owner and avoids retrying partial messages.

The accept loop obtains an owned connection permit before accepting and moves it to the child handler. This bounds active handlers. An OS backlog entry does not count as application admission.

The handler sends its request through bounded mpsc. The pool manager receives another request only while its `JoinSet` has fewer than `active_workers` children. It acquires a worker permit immediately and moves it to the `spawn_blocking` closure. The closure owns it until returning or panicking. A timeout in the async waiter cannot release it.

The manager retains each blocking JoinHandle through its bounded JoinSet and collects the result. The worker can reply through a oneshot, but the deadline may have passed or the client may have disconnected. Either way, the manager must join. Responses carry a tag: `O || payload` for success, `E` for domain error, `J` for a panic or a cancelled closure, or `I` for a manager invariant violation. The report keeps the full JoinError without needing to clone it.

## Shutdown

The owner stops accepting, drops the listener, joins accepted handlers, and then drops the last mpsc sender. The receiver drains queued jobs and joins all started blocking jobs. A fatal accept error uses the same cleanup. User callbacks run only inside spawn_blocking closures, where a panic becomes the worker's JoinError. If the manager itself fails, the report distinguishes unstarted jobs from started closures that may remain unjoined. That report cannot confirm a complete shutdown.

## Rejected shortcuts

- An unbounded channel moves overload into memory.
- A task per request waiting on a semaphore creates an unbounded task queue.
- Timing out a JoinHandle or dropping its waiter allows a started blocking closure to keep running.
- Aborting during normal shutdown can hide whether cleanup finished and whether the permit tracked actual work.
- Resetting the deadline on every read lets a client hold a connection indefinitely.

## Boundaries

Use this package only on IPv4 loopback. Its scope excludes TLS, authentication, telemetry, deployment, retries, and transactional rollback of effects. The processor contract requires finite work. Long-running work needs its own cooperative stop protocol. The report grows with request count, so production use needs a streaming or retention decision.

# Async lending contracts

This TCP service supplement examines the boundary between a borrowed result and work sent to a task.

## Ownership and suspension

\`\`\`text
PacketSource --receive()--> ReceiveFuture --Pending--> wake
      |                         |
      |                         +-- Ready(BorrowedPacket<'source>)
      |                                      |
      |                         callback borrows bytes and awaits
      |                                      |
      +<-------------------------- commit() only after callback Ready
\`\`\`

`BorrowedPacket` holds an exclusive borrow of the source. Dropping it after `Pending` or returning a callback error leaves the cursor unchanged. Only `commit` after callback completion records progress. Later cancellation leaves any effect already performed by the callback in place.

`owned_report_future(ReportSource)` moves only owned data and returns `Future + Send + 'static`, so it can enter `tokio::spawn`. The separate `BoxedReportProvider<'a>` adapter stores providers of different types with a local lifetime at the cost of boxing and dynamic dispatch. A trait with a family of result types does not automatically support dyn.

## Limits

The package caps a record at 4096 bytes and the input at 32 records, and visits records sequentially. The contract test polls a borrowed callback to Pending, checks that an effect persists after Drop, and retries the same record without undoing earlier commits. Its scope excludes transactional rollback of callback effects, exactly-once execution, and cancellation of arbitrary blocking work.

# Mini grep

This educational package uses Rust 2024 and only the standard library. It searches files and directories for a literal, nonempty UTF-8 substring.

`mini-grep [-C N] [--] QUERY PATH...`

Pass `-C` at most once before the query. `N` consists of unsigned ASCII digits and must be in 0–16. `--` ends option parsing. The process exits with 0 when it finds a match, 1 when a valid search finds no matches, and 2 for usage, I/O, format, or limit errors. Errors go to stderr.

## Data contract

- The query must contain 1–1024 bytes. Each line can span at most 65536 raw bytes before LF, counting CR. A CR immediately before LF is removed from the text.
- A final line without LF is processed. Invalid UTF-8 or NUL makes the file invalid.
- The output is the union of context windows in line-number order, with duplicates removed. Each record has the form `label:line:text\n`.
- Directories are visited depth-first after sorting their entries by `PathBuf`. The program processes path arguments in the given order and rereads repeated arguments.
- The limits are 4096 visited entries, depth 32, and 1048576 bytes of retained selection content. Count the text plus one byte per selected line, including empty lines. Each successive file gets only the remaining budget. A separate 1048576 bytes covers rendered stdout, including labels and line numbers. These caps apply to logical content. Heap use also includes Vec storage, paths, the raw line, context, and the rendering buffer. The program assembles all stdout before writing, so an input or limit error leaves no partial stdout. A failure of the stdout device can leave a partial write.

## Running the workshop

```sh
cargo fmt --check
cargo check --locked
cargo test --locked
cargo test --doc --locked
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo run -- -C 1 needle ./fixtures
```

The property test checks selection against a small independent oracle. A separate nightly libFuzzer harness for maintainers exercises queries and contents. It adds no runtime dependency, and its results cover only the exercised inputs.

# ADR — literalny tekst, bufor wyniku i.en:
# ADR — Literal text, buffered output, and symlink rejection

## Decision

Mini grep matches literal text with `str::contains`. Regular expressions and globs are outside its contract. The library separates pure selection, bounded reads, traversal, rendering, and CLI argument parsing. It assembles up to 1 MiB of output before writing to stdout.

## Rationale

A literal query lets us test context, UTF-8, and I/O limits independently of regular-expression syntax. Buffering ensures that an error on a later path cannot mix partial records with diagnostics.

All files share the retained-content budget. The next file gets only what remains of the 1 MiB cap. Vec metadata, paths, context, the raw line, and the final String consume additional heap memory.

## Consequences

GNU grep compatibility is outside the design. Mini grep rejects symlinks and special files and limits depth and entry count. The output cap does not make writes atomic when the stdout device itself fails. See THREAT-MODEL.md for path boundaries.

# Threat model ścieżek\n\nMini grep prze.en:
# Path threat model

Mini grep processes local paths supplied by the process owner and runs without elevated privileges. It checks the final component of each encountered path with `symlink_metadata` and rejects symlinks. Recursion never descends into symlinks. Special files are rejected. Entry and depth limits bound traversal and the buffer used to sort a single directory.

Paths can change between `symlink_metadata` and `File::open`. A symlink in a parent component or a replaced directory can go undetected. Modifying a file while it is being read can change the observed result. These checks provide neither sandboxing nor a snapshot. I/O errors preserve the original `io::Error` as `Error::source`.

Output path labels escape LF, CR, TAB, colons, and backslashes. Paths containing invalid UTF-8 use lossy display, so the original path cannot always be recovered from a label.

# Protocol design worksheet

The starter leaves room to define the text frame contract and migration. Before changing code, specify rules for fields, bytes, frame termination, versions, and unknown data. The contract tests show which decisions must remain stable for older clients.

# Protokół\n\nRamka jest jednym zakończo.en:
# Protocol

A frame is one LF-terminated, tab-delimited record. Version 1 has the form `1	SOURCE	KEY	LEVEL	MESSAGE
`. Version 2 inserts `CORRELATION` before the message. Identifiers contain 1 to 32 bytes using ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. The message is nonempty UTF-8, at most 2048 bytes, without tabs or line breaks.

In version 2, `-` denotes absent correlation. Version 1 carries no correlation field. Its encoder rejects any event that has one. An unknown version, extra fields, invalid UTF-8, an oversized frame, or a missing line terminator is a protocol error.

# Threat model

# Procedura operacyjna\n\n- Przy błędzie.en:
# Runbook

- On a validation failure, retain the error code without the input contents.
- If the queue is full, return an explicit busy signal without creating an unbounded wait.
- If a response is lost, retry with the same key and content. Verify the receipt after the retry.
- For an oversized frame, close the connection after the error response.
- During shutdown, account for accepted, completed, and outstanding work separately.
- Exercise a saturated queue with a bounded test. Verify `QUEUE_FULL` and confirm that no waiting job was created.
- When the store is locked, verify `BUSY`, check for the absence of a partial write, and retry with the same key.
- For a lost response, retry the same content, keep both signals, and record Unknown until the receipt is verified.
- For input above the limit, confirm `TOO_LARGE` and that no row was written.
- If shutdown exceeds its time limit, retain the `drain_overdue` report and verify that the worker was joined before the process exited.

# ADR 0002 — Storage ownership and shutdown

One owner of the SQLite connection receives commands through a bounded queue. The service waits for that owner to finish before producing the final report. A timeout while waiting does not confirm completion.

Multiple workers can improve throughput, but they complicate ordering, limits, and accounting. One worker with bounded mpsc makes ownership and drain behavior testable.

The new files demonstrate a local client with a bounded budget. The parser distinguishes a receipt, refusal, transport failure, deadline, and unknown response. STORAGE is a terminal Unknown. An earlier lost response keeps the outcome Unknown until a valid receipt arrives. The client retries exactly the same bytes on a new connection and never uses receipt-query. TOO_LARGE is a valid service response even though the old V1 client recognizes fewer errors. QUEUE_FULL and BUSY are retryable only within the shared budget.

# Model boundaries

The process uses trusted policy configuration. Authentication is outside its scope. Public GrantSpec describes data. Only the owner can install effective grants. There is no identity parser, TLS, network, durability, clock, expiration, or distributed revocation. Code inside the boundary module is trusted. Rust privacy and moves constrain safe external consumers of the API.

Cost is a declared number. The cost limit does not bound memory or CPU use or measure payload size. Accepted means the counters include the request. Execution, persistence, and delivery are separate. A caller can drop the authorization witness. Reauthorization does not prevent logical replay. A bounded finite test establishes behavior only for the cases exercised.

The policy rules are an authored exercise contract. See the [Rust Reference on visibility and privacy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/visibility-and-privacy.html), [Rust Book on ownership](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-01-what-is-ownership.html), [checked_add](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.u64.html#method.checked_add), and the [OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html). Those references inform the exercise without establishing OWASP compliance. Description licensed CC BY 4.0.

# Explicit file format upgrade

Implement the body of normalize in src/model.rs.

V1 assigns IDs in row order. Preserve titles, completion states, and duplicates. V2 preserves stored IDs and the NEXT numbering history.

The load and prepare_upgrade functions take bytes and do not write the file. The upgrade example performs a separate, explicit upgrade of the named file. Try it on your own copy of a fixture first.

The upgrade assumes a single writer. Comparing bytes detects a change that already happened. It cannot prevent a later write. The temporary file is created beside the original, and a successful rename over the original completes the upgrade. The program does not synchronize the directory or guarantee durability after power loss. A failure to print the message after rename is a reporting error. The file upgrade has already completed.

The package has no external dependencies. Run from the extracted project directory.

    cargo generate-lockfile --offline
    cargo test --offline --locked
    cargo run --offline --locked --example upgrade -- ścieżka/do/kopii.txt
